q: Is Love Fist a real band?
a: No. Love Fist is a fictional rock band written for GTA Vice City (2002). Its songs "Dangerous Bastard" and "Fist Fury" play on V-Rock and were made for the game.

q: Is Axl Rose really in GTA San Andreas?
a: Yes. Axl Rose voices K-DST's DJ, Tommy "The Nightmare" Smith. Chuck D, George Clinton and Sly and Robbie also voice San Andreas DJs.

q: What radio station is Karl Lagerfeld on in GTA IV?
a: K109 The Studio, GTA IV's disco station. His casting as a DJ made fashion news in 2008.

q: Does the GTA IV radio news react to your missions?
a: Yes. Weazel News bulletins change as the story moves, reporting things like the McReary brothers' deaths after "Blood Brothers". Rockstar's audio team described the system in 2008.

q: Why does Lazlow's character get worse in every GTA?
a: Lazlow told IGN at San Diego Comic-Con that Dan Houser deliberately made the in-game Lazlow sadder and less like him each game. In GTA V, Houser told him he would get to dance in his underwear.
Lazlow left Rockstar in 2020 and joined Dan Houser at Absurd Ventures. Asked in 2025 whether he would appear in GTA VI, he said he doubted it.

q: When did GTA get the radio wheel?
a: With GTA V and GTA Online in 2013. Earlier games used a looping next and previous selector, and the 2021 Definitive Edition trilogy gave the older games a wheel too.

q: Who wrote the fake radio ads in GTA?
a: GTA 2's ads were written by Michael Keillor at DMA Design. From GTA III on, Dan Houser and Lazlow wrote the commercials and Lazlow produced them.
